judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'more favorable terms or treatment with respect to the payment or disposition called for by an arbitration award or judicial decree' is a broad comparative standard with no method of comparison.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The accompanying October 26 letter already forgives the balance after six payments, so what 'more favorable treatment' would add is unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific, dated undertaking to withdraw a named suit; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Implements paragraph 1 of the same memorandum; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the provisions against strikes and disruptions of orderly relationships' does not match any provision by that name, and the closing sentence is garbled ('for any future violations of the aforesaid provisions to seek and obtain').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Acceleration of 'the entire remaining balance' cannot be reconciled with the October 26 letter promising that no further payments will be required after six installments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any major change in its operations which has an impact on a significant number of its NMDU employees' rests on two undefined thresholds, softened only by a single example.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-M.3 requires prior consent for any change in condition, which is a stricter and differently-triggered rule than thirty days' notice of a 'major change'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It directs an arbitrator to write a decision 'interpreting the language of Section 16-M' by reference to an earlier oral opinion and a 1971 award involving a different union — the content is entirely outside the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That the parties needed an arbitrator to interpret 16-M is itself an acknowledgment that the changed-conditions provision does not resolve its own application.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Every memorandum, letter agreement or side agreement shall be continued ... and deemed updated' identifies neither the documents nor what 'updated' does to their terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conflicts with 21-D VIII's supersession of all other Newspoint agreements and with the express expiry dates in 21-B.4 and 21-G.3, and sits uneasily with 17-D's settled-for-the-term clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short preamble; 'is within the terms of the current collective bargaining agreement' is the only interpretive claim.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That self-characterisation matters because paragraphs 1-4 add manning and starting-time commitments beyond the Agreement's text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The arithmetic does not obviously work: two situations of five nights and of four days plus one night make ten shifts, yet the text adds 'one additional shift (a total of 11 shifts)'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-A's Carlstadt floor-operations minimum and 21-D III's manning schedule are the surrounding manning rules; this adds to them without cross-reference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'including but not limited to' opens the assignment list while the last sentence makes one task exclusive to the utility man — a general/specific tension inside one paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-I allows employees to be required to perform any covered operation, and 22-A allocates console and jam-clearing work to the delivery department, so exclusivity to one man is a departure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Several undefined terms — 'Aleo Men', 'normal daily operation', 'provided all areas are properly manned' — carry the operative weight.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The final sentence expressly preserves the Times' obligation to hire from the shape in priority order under Section 4, which shows the drafters saw the interaction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The guarantee runs to 'all regular situation holders as of the date of this agreement' but is then limited to 'the named individuals', although no individuals are named.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-J permits starting-time changes on four days' notice and 20-E.7 gives the Publisher discretion over starting times of excess situation holders, both cut across by this guarantee.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'at the required rate' is undefined, though the trigger and the half-hour are precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-L addresses travel time generally and directs the parties to negotiate an arrangement, of which this looks like one instance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple one-off delivery obligation as of a fixed date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The October 26 letter on posting job descriptions covers the same ground on a continuing basis; complementary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific commitment tied to two named employees' job; the only softness is how long the obligation lasts.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-K requires the Publisher to furnish all delivery equipment, which this is consistent with.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'as it does during the week' fixes the standard by reference to existing weekday practice, which is otherwise unrecorded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-E.2(e)(1) already deals with Albany runs being driven by covered employees; consistent in direction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A concrete, if minimal, obligation with a stated frequency.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Relates to the driving-qualification scheme in 2-E.2 and 14-C but conflicts with nothing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such route shall be filed by in-shop bidding' is a misprint for 'filled', and 'in-shop bidding' is not a defined procedure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-B prescribes posting and filling by seniority among regular situation holders, and other side letters use 'inter-shop bidding' — the terminology is not standardised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'including, but not limited to' opens the list of what must be posted, and 'past practice' supplies the baseline.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The closing sentence that these practices 'do not limit either party's rights' sits awkwardly against 5-J's notice rule and the Supplementary Agreement's starting-time guarantee.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two undefined exceptions — improvements granted 'in exchange for productivity improvements (as determined to the Union's reasonable satisfaction)' or 'diverted from the negotiated pattern package' — control the whole promise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps 3-M's most-favoured-nation machinery running the other way and 21-F.3's comparability promise on The News' pension, without any priority rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the present status quo arbitrator' and 'alternate status quo arbitrator' are not the titles used in the Agreement, which speaks of an Impartial Chairman and Alternate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-G provides that the impartial chairmen's term ends on the Agreement's expiration, which this holdover arrangement contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It locates the arbitrator list in 'Section 16-E.1' when 16-E.2 is the paragraph that creates it — the same mis-citation that runs through Section 16.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-E.2 and 16-E.3 prescribe replacement and striking procedures that this open-ended holdover suspends.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear conditional promise to amend on sixty days' notice, with the Union choosing between two frequencies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It amends 2-N.1's monthly deduction mechanics, so the printed section and the letter say different things until notice is given.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Times is happy to continue our discussions' is not an obligation at all, and the letter fixes no subject-matter outcome.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 17-D says wages and other terms have been settled for the term, which sits oddly with an open commitment to keep discussing pension changes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'providing such transport did not involve the Times in increased costs' is an unmeasured proviso, and the operative promise is only 'agreed to discussion'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 9-B uses the same 'increased cost' escape for bulk deliveries by unit employees, so the drafting is at least consistent in kind.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'If a sufficient number of employees are interested' leaves the condition entirely unquantified, and the middle paragraph is only an agreement to discuss with a bank.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-N and the credit-union checkoff letter deal with payroll deductions under LMRA s.302 constraints, which this program would also engage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All trucks used for over-the-road runs (Long Island routes, news company runs, all other long runs)' closes a specific list with an undefined catch-all, 'all other long runs'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-H.1 requires all motor vehicles to be equipped with heaters and defrosters within thirty days, a broader duty than the seat-heater commitments here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'will not, under any circumstances, require additional payments' is emphatic, but 'the six payments referred to in the Memorandum' does not correspond to anything the Memorandum identifies as six payments.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly contradicts the Memorandum of Understanding's promise to pay the full $177,844 in monthly installments and its acceleration clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The letter as printed is fragmentary — 'Newspoint written agreements.' floats free of its sentence — and 'the 48 inch height from the top of the skid' refers to an award not described.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-D VIII says the Newspoint agreement supersedes all other agreements, memoranda or practices applicable to Newspoint, which is hard to square with a promise to abide by all Newspoint written agreements and awards.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It revives a memorandum that the parties have just deleted, 'should there be a problem in the future arising thereunder' — a condition that is both vague and self-contradictory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A deleted memorandum that nonetheless applies cannot be reconciled with 17-D's settlement of terms or with the general memorandum continuing side agreements 'deemed updated'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the Medill Plan' is nowhere defined or otherwise mentioned, and the only obligation is to post rules of eligibility set by the employer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-H governs the Welfare Fund and 22-F/22-G the Times' company plans; where the 'Medill Plan' sits among them is unexplained.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'for a reasonable period of time designated by the employee' and 'an assignment satisfactory to the Publisher' both leave the Publisher and employee with contestable discretion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-N.2 subjects check-off arrangements to LMRA s.302, which would equally apply here though this letter does not say so.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'prohibits the subcontracting of bargaining unit deliveries except as it may exist pursuant to the contract' is circular — the exception simply refers back to the contract it purports to clarify.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-E freezes methods and extent of delivery, 3-F frees the Publisher on new routes and 2-E.2(d)/(h) permit expansion and discontinuance, so this 'clarification' takes sides in an existing tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'will continue its present practice' leaves the vacation-check obligation undefined, though the annual statement duty is concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-B fixes Times vacation-check tax treatment, and 13-I.1 fixes the contribution base whose shifts are to be reported; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Most obligations are conditioned on an undated future event ('when the planned DEC System is installed and operational'), and the reference to 'credited shifts for which contributions were not made' is opaque.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-I.1 requires contributions for each shift worked in the unit, so a reporting duty premised on credited shifts without contributions points to a gap in that obligation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'except if delayed because of an emergency or Act of God' is a general excuse appended to a precise thirty-day deadline.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-A.1 sets the first-year rates retroactive to March 31, 1981, which this letter implements; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A preamble reciting that the sub-committee 'discussed and agreed upon the following', which leaves open which items are agreements and which are reports of discussion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The items that follow are a mix of promises and mere statements, so this framing sentence has to do real work; it is dated 1978 yet carried into the 1981 book.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reported speech — 'the Union requested ... and was advised that such vans would be ordered' — rather than a promise, so whether it binds is genuinely open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parallel Section B item likewise only records that the Company 'indicated' trucks had been ordered, confirming the ambiguity is systemic in this letter.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'would explore the purchase and use of dehumidifiers' creates no measurable duty and no outcome.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-H.1's undue-hardship and working-condition duty is the operative analogue; this adds nothing enforceable to it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parity obligation is clear, though '(500 or more)' is unattached to any stated unit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-A sets uniform scales across offices, so a plant-to-plant parity promise for a particular task is a narrow overlay on that structure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely a record of what 'the Company indicated'; it states no obligation on anyone.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its inclusion among 'agreed upon' items in the preamble is the tension — a recital sitting inside an operative list.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'sixers' is an undefined trade term and 'in the same percentage as they are currently available' fixes the entitlement by unrecorded present practice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere in the Agreement defines the term or the day-shift baseline, so the obligation is unascertainable from the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'five jobs would be defined when posted' with a bare list of job titles; what 'defined' requires is left open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-B and 21-D VII govern posting of situations at Newspoint, and the job-description letter covers posting content — overlapping but consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agreement to meet and discuss with no subject-matter obligation or deadline.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-D V already allocates commercial work at Newspoint, so the topic is partly governed elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A meeting commitment with a fixed thirty-day period; minimal but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the plant-level settlement expectation in 16-A; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same framing problem as the News letter — items 'discussed and agreed upon' — and the printed text is scrambled by marginalia.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Dated November 3, 1978 yet reproduced in the 1981-84 book, its continued operation depends on the general memorandum continuing side agreements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A concrete commitment to create two identified jobs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-D III(a) provides one console man at Newspoint and 22-A allocates console work at Carlstadt; this adds situations consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific as to days, start time and filling method; 'inter-shop bidding' is the only undefined term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-B provides for filling situations by posting and seniority within the shop, so 'inter-shop bidding' is a procedure the Agreement does not define.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'reviewed within a reasonable time ... but in no event later than sixty days' is bounded, but the review carries no obligation as to outcome.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Supplementary Agreement separately fixes combined floor hires and 43rd Street chauffeur availability, which is where any review would land.
